raw_response:
I am 57, been farming this land for 35 years, never went to school. My father taught me everything, and now I watch what Old Wang and Old Li do — they have good fields and I copy them. If it works on their land, it will work on mine. I don't trust those people from the county who come with papers and talk fancy words. I trust my eyes.

My farm is 10.9 mu. That is not small, but it is not big either. I have 8 people under my roof, but my son and my nephew work in the factory in Handan and send money home. That helps, but I don't want to waste it on the farm. I divide my land like this: 5 mu for cotton, that is my cash crop. The other 5.9 mu I do wheat in winter and then maize in summer, one after another. That is what everyone around here does.

For cotton, I plant guoxinmian — the improved kind, not the old traditional cotton. I learned my lesson ten years ago when I bought cheap seed from the market. The bollworms ate half my crop and I lost so much money I couldn't sleep for a week. Now I buy from the county store. In April I plow with the rotary tiller and put down one big bag of compound fertilizer per mu — 50 kg. When the flowers come out in July, I spread another half bag of urea, about 25 kg per mu. Cotton is hungry, and if you feed it well it feeds you. I irrigate three times from my well, and I spray 12 times total — mostly for bollworms and aphids, plus once for weeds and maybe once for those leaf spots. Last year I only sprayed 10 times and the bugs got ahead of me. Never again. I expect about 600 jin per mu if the weather is fair.

For wheat, I plant in early October right after the maize comes off. I use improved seed, about 30 jin per mu. I spread one bag of compound fertilizer per mu before planting and work it in with the rotary tiller. Then in late March at jointing, if the wheat looks even a little yellow, I spread another half bag of urea. I know some people say that is too much, but I would rather waste some fertilizer than lose the whole crop. A bad harvest is a disaster; wasting fertilizer is just money. I irrigate three times because wheat pays the bills. I spray three times — herbicide once at planting, and twice more for bugs and that rust disease. I expect about 900 jin per mu.

For maize, I have to move fast after wheat harvest in June — sometimes I only have two days. I buy hybrid seed from the store, about 2 jin per mu. You cannot save hybrid seed, everyone knows that. I put one bag of compound fertilizer per mu in the seed furrow at planting. There is no time for topdressing, the season is too short. I usually do no-tillage or one quick pass with the tiller so I can plant immediately. I irrigate twice, because the summer rains usually help. I spray three times for weeds and corn borers. I expect about 1000 jin per mu.

Fertilizer keeps getting more expensive — every bag is real money. But I watch my neighbors. If Old Wang buys more, I think about buying more too. I only hire help during cotton picking season, maybe 4 or 5 days. The rest my family does ourselves. I don't know those numbers and formulas. I know that last year I put down one bag per mu and I got a decent crop. That is good enough for me.
